MTL.head: Close, but the Wild have the slight edge
MTL.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canadiens’ best way to tip it is piling up shots.

MIN.head: Leaning the Wild’s way
MIN.body: Even though Montréal has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. Still, it’s close: the Canadiens can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: A heavyweight meeting
paras: The Canadiens (10-3-3) beat Utah 5-4 in overtime on Thursday, and the Wild have won three straight. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (second in the NHL) and the Habs second in the Atlantic (sixth).

The Wild’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.673), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Canadiens’ (.719 on chances worth .563), largely because they’re 7-4 in one-goal games.

The Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (3rd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). The Canadiens, by contrast, take more penalties than they draw (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Canadiens get into more chippy games than anyone (1st). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (28th), so the Wild keep dangerous shots away, but them give up a lot of them. The Canadiens’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Kirill Kaprizov (16 G / 14 A / 30 P in 18 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is tied for third in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Montréal. Quinn Hughes (6 G / 19 A / 25 P in 18 GP) isn’t far behind, with nine points in his last five games. For the Canadiens, Lane Hutson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Cole Caufield (11 G / 4 A / 15 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL.

Jesper Wallstedt (11-2-3 / .922 SV% in 16 GS) has been terrific for Minnesota and will likely start. Montréal has two options in net: Jacob Fowler (7-1-1 / .925 SV% in 9 GS) and Jakub Dobeš (3-2-2 / .846 SV% in 7 GS). Fowler has started six of their last ten games, but Dobeš got the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

The Canadiens have been without Ivan Demidov, Samuel Montembeault and Mike Matheson for several games.
Joel Eriksson Ek has five goals on chances worth about 9.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
